That's a Vulkan driver crash, which is likely the result of a bug in libvulkan / mesa / LLVM. Neither of which we can fix on our end. I suspect that updating this driver stack (e.g. by upgrading to PopOS 24.04 LTS) would solve this.

It's not a great workaround of course to have to ask people to upgrade their Linux distro, but the state of Vulkan drivers was not that good in 2022.

It could be useful to pinpoint which dev/beta/rc snapshot is the first that makes it crash on your system, so that we can maybe narrow down which change caused it, and maybe find a Godot workaround. You can download earlier snapshots on https://godotengine.org/download/archive/
It might be worth reporting a bug to PopOS too, as this is very likely a bug in the versions of the packages that they have. There might be upstream patches that they can backport to fix it.

> It could be useful to pinpoint which dev/beta/rc snapshot is the first that makes it crash on your system, so that we can maybe narrow down which change caused it, and maybe find a Godot workaround.

It breaks as far back as 4.4-dev1. The stack trace is the same.

> I suspect that updating this driver stack (e.g. by upgrading to PopOS 24.04 LTS) would solve this.

24.04 is currently in alpha, so short of changing to another distro, this is not ideal.

> It breaks as far back as 4.4-dev1. The stack trace is the same.

If you can compile Godot from source and do a [git bisect](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/contributing/workflow/bisecting_regressions.html) between `4.3-stable` (assumed `good`, but you might want to test it again to confirm) and 28a72fa4344befeae251d8e9b11b84acd601a244, you might be able to pinpoint the exact commit that broke support for your versions of the Vulkan/AMD driver stack.
The workaround indeed works for me on 4.4-stable.

> sounds like we're not fully safe there on Linux too, at least with older drivers

Not sure what exactly can be causing it, but we can use the same sub-process check used on Windows on Linux as well.
I've got the same issue on my Ubuntu. Crashes on startup.
@HeavyBro1337 Could you check if #103560 fixes it for you? You can download a Linux editor artifact from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103560/checks.

Perhaps a little hint about the root cause. I checked to see if I could reproduce this on my laptop which has NVidia and Intel switchable graphics (I couldn't), but I did notice that, when checking for Vulkan support from OpenGL, the driver reports that presentation is unsupported:

```
Devices:
  #0: Intel Intel(R) Xe Graphics (TGL GT2) - Unsupported, Integrated
  #1: NVIDIA NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Laptop GPU - Unsupported, Discrete
  #2: Unknown llvmpipe (LLVM 15.0.7, 256 bits) - Unsupported, CPU
```

When running the actual application presentation is supported:
```
Devices:
  #0: Intel Intel(R) Xe Graphics (TGL GT2) - Supported, Integrated
  #1: NVIDIA NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Laptop GPU - Supported, Discrete
  #2: Unknown llvmpipe (LLVM 15.0.7, 256 bits) - Supported, CPU
```

CC @DarioSamo Do you think the lack of presentation support could be responsible for a crash somewhere? Is there anything we do in initialization that would require presentation support?

> CC [@DarioSamo](https://github.com/DarioSamo) Do you think the lack of presentation support could be responsible for a crash somewhere? Is there anything we do in initialization that would require presentation support?

The device will currently fail to initialize at all if presentation isn't supported and only if RenderingDevice was given a Window during its creation. Otherwise, it should be fine.
